issues: The tentacles are separated from the body by a full background row, making them look like loose fragments at 1x rather than articulated squid limbs.
The right and lower body contours end in bright blue without a consistent dark edge, so the silhouette is less robust than typical MM2/MM3 enemies.
The face plate is oversized and boxy, leaving little room for shell structure or a clear mine-like mechanical cue.
The center-top face pixels create an awkward notch and isolated-looking black/white accents rather than a deliberate Capcom-style cluster.
The lower tentacles have inconsistent widths and abrupt right-angle bends; the rightmost limb is especially noisy and weakly attached.
Some likely 8x8 regions combine black, white, pale cyan, and blue, making the metasprite less obviously NES palette-safe.
There is no visible warning-state eye treatment or other visual indication of the proximity-triggered explosion behavior.
fixes: Connect the tentacle roots to the underside with one-pixel black joints, retaining at most a single deliberate gap between separate limbs.
Add a one-pixel black contour along selected parts of the right and lower shell, then remove equal amounts of blue to preserve the dimensions.
Reduce the white face plate by one pixel at each side and use the recovered space for dark cheek brackets or small mechanical shell seams.
Replace the center-top notch with a continuous black brow, or make the white interruption a clean two-pixel symmetric highlight.
Redraw the tentacles as two or three clean, consistently thick clusters: a compact gathered frame and a longer thrust frame.
Repartition the colors by 8x8 tile so each tile uses no more than three opaque colors, dropping pale cyan from face-edge tiles if necessary.
Create a warning frame that replaces the dark pupils with a single NES red and holds for several ticks before the explosion animation.

issues: The broad cyan dome and oversized rectangular white face read more like a modern icon than an MM2/MM3 enemy construction.
The lower tentacles are thin, angular, and visually disconnected from the body; at 1x they resemble scattered bars rather than thrusting squid limbs.
The straight vertical left wall and abrupt unoutlined cyan right edge make the body silhouette feel boxy and unfinished.
The face uses large square eyes with little expression; it does not communicate the threatening mine behavior or a red-warning state.
The shell uses black, white, pale cyan, and bright cyan in a way that feels more four-tone than typical disciplined NES metasprite shading.
The stepped pale highlight across the dome is clean but overly broad and smooth for Capcom's compact, cluster-driven shading.
fixes: Narrow the white face by 2-3 pixels and reshape the dome into a rounder, more mechanical squid mantle with a consistent one-pixel black contour.
Join each tentacle directly to the underside and build them from compact 2-pixel-wide clusters; use two clearly distinct animation poses for gathered and thrust states.
Replace the scattered lower bars with three or four readable tentacle lobes, keeping deliberate one-pixel gaps only between complete limbs.
Outline or dark-cap the exposed right cyan edge so the silhouette does not terminate as a flat color slab.
Reduce the dome highlight to one compact pale-cyan cluster and keep each metasprite region to black plus two functional colors.
Give the eyes smaller pupils and reserve a palette-swap frame with red eye pixels for the pre-explosion warning.
Add a small mechanical seam, vent, or central underside nozzle using existing colors to strengthen the robot-mine identity without adding noise.

issues: The enlarged body uses an inconsistent outline: the upper-left is black-bordered while the right side ends directly in bright blue, unlike typical MM2/MM3 contour control.
The huge rectangular white face dominates the sprite and makes it read more like a floating mask or owl than a mechanical squid.
The eyes are tiny cyan marks inside heavy black boxes, so their expression and intended red-warning flash would be difficult to read at 1x.
The lower tentacles are uneven, angular bars with awkward gaps; the far-right appendage especially looks detached from the body.
Several staircase contours around the dome and side fins feel mechanically generated rather than deliberately clustered.
Black, white, and multiple blues crowd some tile regions, making the palette less disciplined than a typical Capcom enemy sprite.
The sprite lacks a clear mine-like mechanical cue such as a warning lens, seam, fuse detail, or armored shell segmentation.
fixes: Reduce the white face by 2-3 pixels in width and 1 pixel in height, then use the recovered space for a stronger dark shell contour.
Carry a consistent 1-pixel black outline around the right body edge and simplify both side contours into cleaner stepped curves.
Replace each boxed eye with a compact 2x2 or 2x3 eye cluster that can palette-swap cleanly from white or cyan to red.
Attach every tentacle directly to the underside and redesign them as three or four compact tapered limbs with clearly different gathered and thrust animation poses.
Remove the isolated-looking far-right blue bar and merge it into a single outlined tentacle cluster.
Limit each 8x8 region to black plus two body colors and transparency where possible; reserve white for the face and red for the warning frame.
Add one small central warning lens or shell seam to communicate the swimming-mine function without adding noise.

issues: The broad cyan dome and dangling legs read as a generic jellyfish more than a mechanical squid or swimming mine.

fixes: Replace the large white patch with two compact 1-2 px eyes under the dome, with alternate red-eye tiles for the warning flash.
Add a black 1 px face or shell seam across the lower body to separate the robotic head from the tentacle assembly.
Simplify the underside into three clearly separated tentacles, removing the enclosed blue cavities and retaining at least 1 px of background between limbs.
Round the dome with cleaner stepped contours: shorten the flat top and use consistent 1 px stair steps on both shoulders.
Use white or light cyan only as a small top-left highlight, keeping each hardware-sprite region to black plus two body colors.
Create a second animation frame with tentacles gathered inward and a thrust frame with them spread downward or backward.

issues: The cyan domed body and dangling legs read as a small floating squid, but the eyes are not clearly identifiable at 1x.

fixes: Replace the lower-center blue maze with two clearly separated eye pixels or eye blocks, leaving black spacing around each.

Reduce the white body highlight to a compact 2x2 or stepped cluster and restore cyan around it.
Simplify the underside into three distinct tentacle groups with clean one-pixel gaps and fewer internal black notches.

issues: The lower third becomes a dense black-and-cyan knot at 1x; individual tentacles and their thrust direction are unclear.

fixes: Open 1-pixel background gaps between three or four tentacles and simplify each tentacle to one solid cyan cluster with a black outer edge.
Create a clear central face band with two separated 1-pixel eyes; use a red palette swap for the warning frame.
Remove the tiny enclosed cyan pockets in the lower center and replace them with larger contiguous clusters.
Narrow or taper the upper mantle by 1 pixel on each lower side so it reads as a squid body rather than a jellyfish cap.

issues: The enlarged silhouette is lopsided and overcomplicated, especially along the upper-right dome and lower tentacles.

fixes: Reduce the dome to a cleaner, near-symmetrical 12-14-pixel-wide shape with a continuous 1-pixel black outer contour.
Narrow the pink right-side band to a 2-3-pixel accent or move it into a distinct rear propulsion/tentacle cluster.
Create two explicit 2x2 eye clusters under the dome, using black pupils and a shared red/pink flash color.
Delete the detached upper-right pink pixel and any single-pixel notches that do not clarify the silhouette.
Separate the head from the tentacles with a clean horizontal dark line or one-pixel gap.
Simplify the underside to three or four chunky tentacle tips, each built from deliberate 2-pixel clusters rather than long jagged hooks.
Make two animation frames: gathered tentacles tucked beneath the body, then a thrust frame with short, evenly spaced outward tentacles.

issues: The upper-right face has only one ambiguous pale eye mark; at 1x it does not clearly read as a pair of eyes capable of flashing red.

fixes: Delete the detached red pixel and place two adjacent or symmetrically spaced eye pixels inside a clearly bounded black face band.
Reserve red for an alternate alert frame in which both eye pixels change from pale cyan to red; do not scatter red elsewhere.
Simplify the mantle to black plus one main cyan and one highlight color, replacing most of the large pink side patch with the main body color.

Shorten or remove the long right appendage; if retained, curve it downward so it belongs to the tentacle fan rather than reading as a tail.
Remove one-pixel notches and awkward black pockets around the lower center and right edge, favoring 2-3-pixel clusters and stepped Capcom-style curves.
Plan each 8x8 hardware-sprite region around no more than three opaque colors, using a separate overlay sprite only for the flashing eyes if necessary.

issues: At 1x, the mantle, face, and tentacles merge into a busy cyan-pink-black mass; the squid silhouette is not immediate.

Reduce the palette to black, one pale cyan, one stronger cyan or pink accent, and transparency within each sprite tile; use red only in the flashing-eye frame.
Clean the lower contour into deliberate two- and three-pixel runs, eliminating isolated tips and uneven staircase patterns.
Make the mine function readable through animation: neutral cyan eyes, a red-eye warning frame, then a compact bright explosion frame.
